trial_name: ART — Effect of Lung Recruitment and Titrated PEEP vs Low PEEP on Mortality in ARDS (2017)
citation: Cavalcanti AB, Suzumura ÉA, Laranjeira LN, et al; Writing Group for the Alveolar Recruitment for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Trial (ART) Investigators. Effect of lung recruitment and titrated positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) vs low PEEP on mortality in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2017;318(14):1335-1345
one_liner: In early moderate-to-severe ARDS, a strategy of recruitment manoeuvre plus compliance-titrated PEEP increased 28-day mortality compared with a low-PEEP strategy (55.3% vs 49.3%; HR 1.20).

pico.population: Adults with moderate-to-severe ARDS within 72 hours of onset, after standardized ventilation confirmation (PaO2:FiO2 ≤200 mm Hg)
pico.intervention: Maximum recruitment manoeuvre (pressure-controlled, PEEP up to 45 cmH2O) followed by decremental PEEP titration to best respiratory-system compliance, then set PEEP at best compliance +2 cmH2O, with reassessment
pico.comparison: Low-PEEP strategy using ARDSNet PEEP–FiO2 table, no recruitment manoeuvres

background.existing_knowledge: In ARDS, collapsed lung units promote atelectrauma; higher PEEP and recruitment can improve oxygenation but risk haemodynamic compromise and overdistension. Prior trials of higher vs lower PEEP and open lung approaches had mixed results.
background.knowledge_gap: Uncertainty about patient selection and optimal PEEP titration method; physiology-based strategies proposed individualising PEEP after recruitment using respiratory-system compliance.
background.hypothesis: Lung recruitment with compliance-guided higher PEEP would reduce mortality by reducing ventilator-induced lung injury (via improved mechanics and reduced driving pressure).

methods.design: Randomised, multicentre, investigator-initiated, international, open-label, parallel-group trial in 120 ICUs across 9 countries.
methods.setting: 120 ICUs, 9 countries; enrolled patients with ARDS within 72 hours of onset.

inclusion: Berlin-definition ARDS; after 3 hours of standardised ventilation (VT 6 mL/kg PBW, RR ≤35/min, FiO2 1.0, PEEP 10 cmH2O) and a further 30 min at FiO2 1.0 and PEEP 10 cmH2O, required PaO2:FiO2 ≤200 mm Hg.
exclusion: More than 72 hours since ARDS onset; contraindications to recruitment/higher airway pressures (e.g., untreated pneumothorax, bronchopleural fistula); severe haemodynamic instability; intracranial hypertension; severe chronic lung disease; other protocol-defined exclusions.

methods.intervention: Core strategy: maximum recruitment manoeuvre (pressure-controlled, ΔP 15 cmH2O; PEEP 25 for 1 min, 35 for 1 min, 45 for 2 min; target max airway pressure 60 cmH2O) followed by decremental PEEP titration (volume-control VT 5 mL/kg; PEEP from 23 cmH2O down to 11 in steps of 3 cmH2O, each step 4 min, selecting best compliance). Then set PEEP at best compliance +2 cmH2O, with a second recruitment at PEEP 45 for 2 min. After 556th patient, protocol modified: recruitment pressures reduced (PEEP 25, 30, 35 for 1,1,2 min; max airway pressure 50 cmH2O; titration step duration 3 min; final recruitment at PEEP 35 for 2 min). Co-interventions: lung-protective ventilation targets in both groups; rescue therapies permitted.
methods.comparison: Low-PEEP strategy using ARDSNet PEEP–FiO2 table; no recruitment manoeuvres; rescue therapies permitted.
methods.sample_size_power: Event-driven: planned to continue until 520 deaths by 28 days to provide 90% power to detect HR 0.75 with type I error 5%; final α=0.042 due to interim monitoring.
secondary_outcomes: commencement/increase vasopressors or hypotension within 1 hour
methods.follow_up: Mortality to 28 days (primary) and 6 months; in-hospital and ICU outcomes within index admission.

headline_bullets: 28-day mortality higher with recruitment + titrated PEEP (55.3% vs 49.3%; HR 1.20, 95% CI 1.01–1.42, P=0.041).
6-month mortality also higher (65.3% vs 59.5%; HR 1.18, 95% CI 1.01–1.38).
Early harm signal: death ≤7 days 31.9% vs 25.5% (RD 6.4%, P=0.001); barotrauma ≤7 days 5.6% vs 1.6% (P<0.001).
No subgroup showed benefit; harm direction consistent across prespecified strata.

safety: Pneumothorax requiring drainage ≤7 days: 3.2% vs 1.2% (RD 2.0%, 95% CI 0.4–3.7, P=0.03)
Haemodynamic instability (vasopressor initiation/increase or hypotension ≤1 hour): 34.8% vs 28.3% (RD 6.5%, 95% CI 1.0–12.0, P=0.02)
Rescue therapies within 7 days similar (15.6% vs 17.5%); prone positioning 15.2% vs 16.1%.

domains.notes: Central web-based randomisation with permuted blocks (size 4), stratified by ICU, age, and PaO2:FiO2 (≤100 vs >100); allocation concealment credible.
Open-label ventilation strategies; primary outcome (mortality) objective and centrally defined; co-interventions tracked.
1013 randomised; 3 withdrew consent, excluded from analyses; primary analysis sample 1010 (501 vs 509).
480/501 (95.8%) received recruitment manoeuvre; 21/501 (4.2%) did not; protocol modification after 556th patient reduced manoeuvre intensity.
Well balanced (age 51.4 vs 50.8 years; SAPS 3 63.5 vs 62.7; baseline PaO2:FiO2 119.5 vs 117.2 mm Hg; shock 63.5% vs 61.7%).

Clear early separation: at 1 hour, PEEP 16.4 vs 13.0 cmH2O, driving pressure 11.5 vs 13.0 cmH2O, plateau pressure 27.9 vs 25.9 cmH2O; Day 1: PEEP 16.2 vs 12.0, driving pressure 11.7 vs 13.5; Day 3: PEEP 14.2 vs 10.5, driving pressure 12.1 vs 13.5.
Rescue therapies within 7 days similar (15.6% vs 17.5%); prone positioning 15.2% vs 16.1%.
Mortality outcomes clear; safety outcomes included prespecified barotrauma definitions and clinically relevant pneumothorax requiring drainage.
Prespecified interim monitoring and adjusted primary alpha; primary time-to-event analysis with Cox model; secondary outcomes interpreted as exploratory.

internal_validity.verdict: Internal validity moderate-to-strong: robust randomisation, clear separation of ventilator strategy, objective primary endpoint, though open-label delivery and mid-trial protocol modification introduce complexity.

domains.notes: Adults with moderate-to-severe ARDS early in syndrome, enrolled across diverse international ICUs; pneumonia most common risk factor, high septic shock prevalence.
Applies to early moderate-to-severe ARDS in ICUs capable of protocolised recruitment and haemodynamic monitoring; limited for very unstable patients or resource-constrained settings.
Patients with contraindications to high airway pressures, severe haemodynamic instability, or other protocol-defined safety exclusions may limit application to the most unstable phenotypes.
Protocolised recruitment and decremental titration require experienced staff and close haemodynamic monitoring; feasibility may be limited in resource-constrained settings.

external_validity.verdict: External validity good for early moderate-to-severe ARDS in well-resourced ICUs; generalisability limited for unstable patients or settings without intensive monitoring.

strengths: Large, international, multicentre ARDS ventilation trial with patient-centred primary outcome.
Early ARDS enrolment with standardised eligibility confirmation to reduce misclassification.
Protocolised and clearly separated ventilator strategies with objective primary endpoint.
Preplanned interim monitoring and time-to-event primary analysis.
limitations: Open-label intervention with potential for performance bias (mitigated for mortality but relevant for process outcomes).
Mid-trial protocol modification after safety concerns, potentially introducing treatment heterogeneity over time.
Complex intervention bundle (recruitment + titration + repeated manoeuvres) limits attribution of harm/benefit to individual components.
Control strategy PEEP levels may be higher than 'low PEEP' in some historic comparators, affecting interpretation of the counterfactual.

critical_appraisal.summary: ART is a large, well-conducted trial that demonstrated harm from aggressive recruitment manoeuvres plus compliance-titrated PEEP in early moderate-to-severe ARDS, with increased mortality and safety signals; internal validity is moderate-to-strong, and external validity is good for similar ICU settings.
weaknesses: Complex intervention bundle limits mechanistic attribution
Control PEEP may not represent lowest PEEP

sections.authors_conclusion: Routine use of aggressive recruitment manoeuvres combined with compliance-guided PEEP titration in early moderate-to-severe ARDS increased mortality and should not be adopted as standard care.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: Do not use routine aggressive recruitment manoeuvres with compliance-titrated PEEP in early moderate-to-severe ARDS; this strategy increases mortality.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Adults with early moderate-to-severe ARDS (PaO2:FiO2 ≤200 mm Hg) within 72 hours of onset, managed in ICUs.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: Higher PEEP without recruitment manoeuvres is harmful; the trial tested a specific recruitment + titration strategy, not higher PEEP alone.
implementation_caveats: If recruitment manoeuvres are used, they should be brief, low-pressure, and with careful haemodynamic monitoring.
Prioritise proven ARDS interventions (e.g., prone positioning, lung-protective ventilation) over recruitment manoeuvres.
Consider higher PEEP without recruitment in moderate-to-severe ARDS per current guidelines.

controversies.notes: Editorial emphasised that intensity of recruitment/PEEP and early haemodynamic/barotrauma signals provide plausible mechanisms for increased mortality, tempering enthusiasm for open lung strategies.
Correspondence argued that selecting PEEP by best compliance may not reliably identify safe PEEP, potentially permitting overdistension despite improved compliance metrics.
Correspondence highlighted implementation complexity and questioned whether manoeuvre timing/intensity contributed to harm in real-world delivery.
Correspondence noted that eligibility confirmation and manoeuvre phases used FiO2 1.0, raising concern that hyperoxia could amplify ventilator-induced lung injury during high-stress manoeuvres.
Investigators responded addressing protocol design, feasibility/training, and alternative mechanistic explanations (including breath stacking and lung-protective features of control strategy).
Published statistical analysis plan clarified outcome handling, underscoring importance of prospectively specified analysis frameworks.
PHARLAP halted enrolment after ART and reported no improvement in ventilator-free days or mortality, with increased cardiovascular adverse events, aligning with safety-limited benefit–harm profile.

Bayesian network meta-analysis suggested higher PEEP without recruitment had highest probability of mortality benefit, while higher PEEP with prolonged recruitment had high probability of harm, concordant with ART.

ESICM guidelines recommend against prolonged high-pressure recruitment manoeuvres and against routine brief recruitment manoeuvres; ATS guideline update suggests higher PEEP without recruitment and recommends against prolonged recruitment manoeuvres (strong recommendation).

context_related_trials.relation: Phase II maximal recruitment open lung strategy halted after ART; reported no improvement in ventilator-free days or mortality, with increased cardiovascular adverse events, supporting safety concerns.

unresolved_questions: Optimal method for PEEP titration in ARDS remains uncertain.
Role of brief, low-pressure recruitment manoeuvres in specific subgroups (e.g., severe hypoxaemia) not addressed.
Whether higher PEEP without recruitment improves outcomes in moderate-to-severe ARDS is still debated, though guidelines conditionally recommend it.

quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: Avoid aggressive recruitment manoeuvres with compliance-titrated PEEP in ARDS; use higher PEEP without recruitment if needed, per guidelines.
